thread:
maria_sales: MediCore wants a Private deployment POC. Requirements: TGW-based multi-account routing, no internet egress from app subnets, but models must be pulled from a central S3 account. Also need to avoid long-lived API keys in their infra. Any architecture notes?

devon_se: Are they asking for Redwood Private (VPC in their account) or for us to expose a PrivateLink service?

maria_sales: They prefer control plane in their VPC (Private deployment) but are open to PrivateLink for control-plane calls if it's easier. Security is strict about asymmetric routing / unexpected egress.

jun_eng: Recommend TGW + explicit-egress VPC pattern: attach customer app VPCs to TGW with route table pointing 0.0.0.0/0 to a single egress VPC (where NATs/firewalls live). Keeps app subnets with no direct internet. For model pulls from our model S3 account, either: 1) allow VPC endpoint to S3 with cross-account bucket policy, or 2) route to egress VPC and use an outbound proxy that has cross-account access.

jun_eng: Example TGW route table entries (app-vpc attachment):
```
# TGW route table for app-vpc attachment
0.0.0.0/0 -> attachment: tgw-attach-explicitegress (egress VPC)
10.20.0.0/16 -> attachment: vpc-app
arn:aws:ec2:... -> propagate: disabled
```

sam_sre: Important ops notes: - Disable route propagation from transit attachment if you want explicit control. - If you use NAT instances, ensure source/dest check disabled. NAT Gateway is simpler. - For interface endpoints (PrivateLink) ensure SGs allow traffic from our management subnets.

caroline_security: Security checklist items we'll need from their infra team: diagram, list of CIDRs, a commitment that app instances won't have public IPs, and how they want key rotation for any credentials we provide. Also need to know whether they require HSM-backed KMS for keys.

devon_se: PrivateLink option for control plane: we can front our control-plane services with an NLB + EndpointService in our account. Customer creates an Interface Endpoint (VPCE) to that service. Pros: simpler TLS to our NLB and controlled access. Cons: does NOT automatically cover S3 model downloads — you'll still need either VPC S3 endpoint with cross-account bucket policy or route via egress VPC.

maria_sales: They also asked if we can avoid long-lived Dedicated pool keys — can we hand out a short-lived session token for the POC?

jun_eng: Yes. We support a bootstrap token flow: engineer requests a one-time bootstrap token (expires 10m) and exchanges it for short-lived session creds that are scoped to the Dedicated pool for the POC. Example exchange:
```bash
# exchange bootstrap token for session creds
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.internal/v1/bootstrap/exchange \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bootstrap_token": "<one-time-token>", "scope": "dedicated:pool:medicore-poc"}'
```

ticket-bot: Support ticket created: #INC-76543 - POC MediCore: TGW + PrivateLink checklist -> https://support.redwood/INC-76543

sam_sre: Next steps from infra side: I'll draft a topology diagram showing TGW + explicit-egress VPC + interface endpoint for control-plane. Devon — please confirm which subnets we should publish NLB in (2 AZs minimum). Maria — I'll attach diagram to the ticket.

maria_sales: :thumbsup: assigning to me. I'll set up a sync with MediCore infra lead for Wednesday 10am PT and add the security checklist items to the ticket.
